standard_prerequisites.name: Open mapping lemma
standard_prerequisites.use: The continuous map u is open, hence surjective.

core_obligations: Set F^n = Ker(M → H^p(X,F_n)) and observe I F^n ⊂ F^{n+1}, so the I-adic topology is finer than the limit topology (proof lines 9081-9089).

Build the graded submodule ⊕E_n ⊂ ⊕H^p(X, I^nF_{n+1}) with E_n the inverse image of F^n/F^{n+1}, verify the graded map ⊕E_n → ⊕F^n/F^{n+1}, use ACC to pick finitely many homogeneous generators and lifts a_i ∈ F^{c_i} (the grading verification is summarized as details omitted in the source at line 9101) (proof lines 9090-9113).

Claim IF^n = F^{n+1} for n ≥ c: from the generators get F^{n+1} = F^{n+2} + IF^n, deduce F^{n+1} = F^{n+e} + IF^n for all e > 0 so IF^n is dense in F^{n+1}, then apply the open mapping lemma to u : (F^n)^⊕r → F^{n+1} to get surjectivity and conclude F^{n+c} ⊂ I^nM (proof lines 9114-9135).
proof_roadmap: Compare the two topologies through the kernels F^n.
Get finite generation of the graded quotients from ACC.
Prove IF^n = F^{n+1} for large n with the open mapping lemma.
difficulty_reason: Two-direction comparison: the I-adic topology is finer via IF^n ⊂ F^{n+1}; the converse uses finite generation of the graded module ⊕E_n, generators a_i ∈ F^{c_i}, and the open mapping lemma applied to the continuous map (F^n)^⊕r → F^{n+1}.
